status: provisional; not calibrated on real papers
scorer: deterministic code (checks/score.py), not a model self-rating

implementation_agreement.sample_identity: identical sorted list of respondent IDs in the estimation sample
implementation_agreement.rule: Compare A, B and C pairwise on sample identity, N and origin estimates before any target comparison. Two agreeing implementations permit scoring on that pair; the third goes to code audit. No agreeing pair -> indeterminate/implementer_disagreement.
implementation_agreement.justification: Same OLS problem on the same numeric file is deterministic up to floating-point error; 1e-6 is far above double-precision round-off for these magnitudes and far below printed precision (0.001).

rounding.coefficients_and_se: printed to 3 decimals; published interval = printed value +/- 0.0005

sign: Assessable only when the published coefficient's rounding interval excludes zero; a reconstructed estimate of opposite sign is a sign failure.

inference.tail: one-tailed in the hypothesized (positive) direction for HRM-practice claims, per the article's stated tests; controls and two-sided claims use the article's printed rule
inference.band_difference: integer distance between published star band and reconstructed band
inference.discrepancy_criterion: band change of 2 or more (adjacent-band change never sufficient)
inference.positive_claim_rule: For a claim of positive significance, a stronger reconstructed band is not a failure. For a claim of non-significance, a reconstructed significant result in either direction is recorded as contradicting it.

direction_by_tier.hrm_and_interaction_terms: upper tail (hypothesized positive) for printed-significant cells; for printed non-significant cells the band is computed from min(upper, lower) one-tailed p and any reconstructed band index <= 1 (p<.05) counts as contradicting non-significance with distance 3 - band
direction_by_tier.controls: one-tailed p in the direction of the printed estimate
direction_by_tier.F_tests: upper-tail F p value; printed stars map to the same bands

inference.band_distance: For printed-significant cells: d = max(0, recon_band - pub_band) with bands 0:p<.01, 1:.01-.05, 2:.05-.10, 3:>=.10 (stronger reconstruction is not a failure). For printed non-significant cells: d = 3 - recon_band (two-or-more = discrepant criterion).

magnitude.justification: Same public NOS release but independently constructed multi-item scales and an incompletely documented sample rule; differences up to two sampling SEs are treated as within reconstruction noise. Provisional, not calibrated.
not_audited: (Intercept) (depends on dummy offsets and scale origins)
PCTMGR (percentage vs proportion unit ambiguity; algebraic check only)

n_tolerance.consequence: N mismatch makes the origin sample criterion unmet: the claim cannot be classified consistent; it becomes indeterminate/sample_reconstruction unless the discrepant rule is met at the origin and at every equivalent reading, in which case it is a discrepant candidate requiring adversarial review and human confirmation.

benchmark_inference.benchmark_adaptation: Organizations are the sampling and observation unit; no assignment-level clustering applies, so no clusters are invented. Declared adaptation: HC3 heteroskedasticity-consistent SEs (Long & Ervin 2000, The American Statistician 54:217-224) as the benchmark for linear models. Wild cluster bootstrap not applicable (no clusters). Few-cluster threshold not applicable.
benchmark_inference.fragile_inference: Coefficient reproduces (magnitude within 1.0 SE, same sign, band difference <= 1 under native SEs) but the HC3 benchmark band is 2 or more bands weaker than the published band, or crosses from p<.05 to p>=.10.
benchmark_inference.status: declared adaptation: HC3 (no assignment-level clusters); not a wild cluster bootstrap

report: share significant at one-tailed .05 in hypothesized direction
equivalent_set_summary.stability_rule_fragile: Origin matches, and among substantive equivalent specifications either sign agreement share < 0.80 or (for a claim of positive significance) the share significant at one-tailed .05 < 0.50
equivalent_set_summary.uncertain_set: reported separately; does not enter the fragility rule

grey_zone: Benefit of uncertainty goes to indeterminate. Discrepant requires: implementations agree; origin outside tolerance on sign, a >=2-band inference change, or large magnitude; the same holds at every equivalent reading; survives adversarial review; human confirmation recorded. Without human confirmation the record reads discrepant_candidate_pending_human_review.
missingness_failure: Failed fits are retained with reasons; a claim whose origin model fails in all implementations is not_attemptable for that scope.

paper_aggregation.focal_structure: H1 primary focal (both readers designate H1 as the headline claim); H2 also focal (both readers).
mapping: fully_reproduced: H1 consistent and H2 consistent and no lower-tier discrepant_candidate
partially_reproduced: H1 consistent and (H2 discrepant or any lower-tier/secondary discrepant_candidate)
indeterminate: H1 or H2 indeterminate (sub-codes carried)
fragile_inference (H1) reported as its own category, not mapped
paper_aggregation.qualification: Every cell and claim outcome is retained; no fraction of matching cells is used as a success rate.

calibration_status: Provisional constants; synthetic rule tests in checks/test_score.py only. Planted-error, null-data, unreachable-target, post-cutoff and human-reproduced arms not performed (outside single-paper session).
cell_outcome: 1. not_attemptable: origin fit failed in every implementation.
2. indeterminate/implementation_disagreement: no two implementations agree on sample identity and origin estimates within tolerance.
3. Criteria at origin on the agreeing pair: sign, band distance d, magnitude m (published-SE units).
4. discrepant_criteria = sign failure OR d >= 2 OR m > 2.0.

5. If discrepant_criteria at origin AND at every successfully fitted grid specification (no substantive equivalent set exists, so all uncertain deviations are required to agree before discrepancy is asserted): discrepant_candidate (needs adversarial review and human confirmation; otherwise reported as discrepant_candidate_pending_human_review).
6. If discrepant_criteria at origin but at least one uncertain deviation is within tolerance: indeterminate/label_sensitive.
7. Else if family N mismatch (> 5% from sealed N): indeterminate/sample_reconstruction.
8. Else if HC3 benchmark band is 2+ bands weaker than published band (printed-significant cells) or crosses from p<.05 to p>=.10: fragile_inference.
9. Else consistent (within tolerance on all assessable criteria; magnitude band within/moderate reported).

H1.primary_cells: HRM-term coefficients in org_M2, org_M3, mkt_M7, mkt_M8 printed with a positive estimate and a star (10 cells)
H1.secondary_cells: remaining HRM-term coefficients in those models (14 cells)
rule: not_attemptable if all primary cells not_attemptable
discrepant if >= 6 of 10 primary cells discrepant_candidate
else indeterminate if any primary cell indeterminate (sub-codes carried)
else fragile_inference if >= 6 primary cells fragile_inference
else consistent if every primary cell consistent or fragile_inference (minority)

H2.primary_cells: interaction-block F for org_M4, org_M5, mkt_M9, mkt_M10 (printed non-significant)
rule: discrepant if >= 3 of 4 primary cells discrepant_candidate
else indeterminate if any primary cell indeterminate

lower_tiers.diagnostic: R2, overall F, HRM-block F (org_M2, org_M3, mkt_M7, mkt_M8)
